data.narrative:
Fractile is a Series B semiconductor company that has raised $220M to date, operating within a competitive frontier-chip sector anchored by 3 public comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers spanning stages from Series A through late growth.

Two valuation methods are applicable given available data. Stage-progression analysis, which applies a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier from Series B forward momentum to the $220M capital base, yields $418M. Peer-median benchmarking across 5 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—including Positron AI ($1.0B at Series B), d-Matrix ($2.0B at Series C), Etched ($5.0B at Series C), SambaNova Systems ($11.0B at Series A), and DEEPX ($529M at Series C)—produces a $2.0B median with a range of $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (21.5x median across the semiconductor tickers) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue.

Triangulation across the two applicable methods yields a valuation range of $355M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide dispersion reflects genuine heterogeneity in peer maturity and performance within the frontier-chip space. Key uncertainties include revenue scale (undisclosed), the relevance of stage-heterogeneous peers, and whether Fractile's technical positioning justifies valuation toward the peer median versus the lower stage-progression estimate.
